    Where is measurable activity concentrated?

    National Sum of Lights grew -0.0% per year between 2015 and 2024. The light-to-population elasticity across ADM2 units is 1.49 (95% CI 1.21–1.76, R²=0.14): light concentrates faster than people, a signature of agglomeration.

    Who lives without detectable light?

    138,332,168 people — 63.9% of the inhabited population — live in cells that are inhabited but emit no detectable night-time light, against 121,861,105 in 2015. The largest concentrations are listed in the table; they are the natural starting point for a targeted off-grid or grid-extension programme. Depending on the noise floor (0.15–0.5 nW·cm⁻²·sr⁻¹), this figure ranges from 135,638,736 to 143,921,872: that is the indicator's real uncertainty.

    How did the lit footprint change?

    The lit footprint moved from 45,104 to 52,274 km² (+15.9%), with 19,798 km² newly lit and 12,628 km² losing detectable light. The sprawl ratio of 158972129.20 indicates a pattern of outward spread rather than densification.

    Lit-footprint transition between the two dates

    Is light concentrating or spreading?

    Population-weighted inequality in light per capita across ADM2 units narrowed from 0.821 to 0.775 (Gini). 50% of total inequality sits between ADM1 regions and 50% within them. Initially dimmer units grew faster, indicating convergence.

    Lorenz curve of light against population

    Growth against initial level (β-convergence)

    Which districts changed significantly?

    Median ADM2 growth in Sum of Lights is +3.7% per year. Growth is measured between the median of the first and last three years. 41 unit(s) exceed the robust +2.5σ threshold and 32 fall below −2.5σ; these are candidates for investigation, not confirmed findings — each should be checked against the gas-flare list, the product version and any known local event. 0 unit(s) with a very low initial base are shown but never flagged. Neighbouring districts grow alike (Moran's I = 0.12): flagged changes often cluster and should be read as regional rather than local phenomena.

    Any month-level anomaly?

    Monthly Sum of Lights shows a seasonal amplitude of 2.38× between the brightest and dimmest calendar month — a reminder that month-on-month comparisons are meaningless without seasonal adjustment. 45 observation(s) deviate by more than 2.5 robust sigma from their own month-of-year baseline.

    Does the proxy survive official statistics?

    Dissemination verdict
    EXPERIMENTAL
    Publishable only as an EXPERIMENTAL statistic, clearly labelled as such and presented alongside the official source it complements. Reason: no independent official statistic: the correlation with population is a consistency check, not a validation.

    Rank correlation with independent statistics

    Method in one paragraph

    Limitations — read before citing

    • Thresholds: noise floor 0.25, urban core 10.0 nW·cm⁻²·sr⁻¹; every 'unlit' figure depends on the first of these.
    • The brightest 1 % of pixels hold 83.4% of the national Sum of Lights.
    • Gas-flare candidates detected: 20. Verify against petroleum infrastructure before interpreting.
    • Night-time lights do not measure electricity access, GDP or population — every such reading is an inference.
    • Activity that emits no light is invisible here: subsistence agriculture, daytime informal trade, indoor activity.
    • No DMSP-OLS year is compared with a VIIRS year; the two are different physical quantities.
